# macOS bridge initialization failure (November 2026)

The installed 0.7.0.15 plugin appeared in Stream Deck, and its macOS watcher was running, but the watcher repeatedly timed out enabling Codex Micro. The diagnostic reported `enabled:[true]`, `detected:null`, `nativeEventBus:false`, and `deviceHandlers:0`. A bridge state file existed, but its presence alone did not establish a working bridge. The observed log contained this failure from at least October 21 through November 2. macOS reported version 27.2. The Codex app version could not be read in the sandbox.

The runtime override searched only a fixed set of renderer module names for the native event bus. Upstream [PR #16](https://github.com/dazer1234/codex-stream-deck/pull/16) reports that newer Codex builds expose it in `app-shared-*` and validates that change on Windows. Including `app-shared` in discovery and verification restored initialization on this Mac: the live renderer reported one device handler, successful device-event dispatch, and one each of the HID and joystick handlers. After installing the updated watcher, its log confirmed that it reused the healthy bridge. Individual Stream Deck actions were not exercised in that check.

Restarting Stream Deck did not restore the keys. The installed plugin logged `Codex Micro slot signals are not loaded` and reported local health as degraded. The resolver-shaped exports in `app-shared-*` were unrelated. Codex 26.1027.61615 (24141) still ships the slot module, but did not load it automatically. The macOS watcher now discovers the versioned filename from the bounded ASAR index and passes it to the plugin through bridge state. With this change, the snapshot reader returned six populated slots from the live renderer. Verify actual Stream Deck rendering and key presses separately; a successful snapshot alone is not full acceptance.

For a recurrence, inspect `~/Library/Application Support/CodexDeck/watcher.log` and compare the installed watcher with the launcher source. After building and installing an updated watcher using the macOS instructions, check for successful initialization and exercise the configured keys. Avoid restarting Codex during active work; a recovery restart can interrupt sessions. Do not include bridge state files or personal paths in public bug reports.

## Numbered renderer bundles (November 5)

Codex 26.1029.61003 replaced the named renderer chunks with numbered Rspack bundles. The loopback connection still worked, but the watcher could no longer discover the event bus and the plugin reported `Codex Micro slot signals are not loaded`. The slot module was no longer present under its previous filename, so scanning the archive index could not restore it.

The shared renderer discovery now reads the entry module's exported `__webpack_require__` cache. It inspects initialized exports without executing unloaded factories, ignores failed modules and inaccessible exports, and identifies the Micro slot namespace from its native snapshot fields. The legacy ESM discovery and macOS archive-index fallback remain available. Snapshot reads, native input dispatch, standalone keycaps, and reset-client discovery use the same module lookup. Reset credits were not consumed during verification.

On the updated macOS app, initialization and verification both reported ready with one HID and one joystick handler. The snapshot returned six populated slots, and standalone keycap registry/command-runner discovery succeeded without executing a command. After installing the updated watcher and plugin locally as 0.7.0.20 and restarting Stream Deck, its XL desktop preview showed the six task keys again. Physical key presses opened the expected chats, but logs exposed false activation errors because inactive composers remain mounted. Active-thread detection now prefers the native active sidebar row and falls back only to a visible composer. A live native press/release test activated another task and restored the original task successfully. This follow-up was installed locally as 0.7.0.21. Recent-mode ordering remains owned by Codex; use pinned or individual assignments when fixed positions are needed.
